# Implementation-Readiness Checklist: Transport-Independent Core Kernel

**Purpose**: Validate the *quality* of the Phase 002 requirements and plan artifacts — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage — before tasks are generated. This is a unit-test suite for the English, not for the code.
**Created**: 2026-08-16
**Resolved**: 2026-08-16 (post-`/speckit-analyze` remediation round)
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [research.md](../research.md) | [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

> **Scope note.** [requirements.md](./requirements.md) validates the **specification** against the
> `/speckit-specify` item set and stands at 16/16. This checklist is **separate and additive**: it
> examines the **plan-stage artifacts** — research decisions, contracts, the crate DAG, and the
> governance gates — for the same qualities. Neither file replaces the other, and no item here was
> copied from there.

> **Interaction record.** The skill directs up to three clarifying questions. Each was individually
> unambiguous from the request and is therefore **derived and recorded rather than asked**, because
> the surrounding instruction runs this stage through to `/speckit-analyze` without stopping:
> **focus** — the six areas were named explicitly; **depth** — *formal gate*, since the constitution
> makes phase-level review mandatory and FR-035 blocks a merge on an ADR; **audience and timing** —
> the reviewer at pull request, plus the maintainer who must personally decide the ADR-0007 gate,
> applied **before** `/speckit-tasks`. If any derivation is wrong, the affected items are the ones
> to reopen.

> **Resolution record.** All 46 items are now resolved with a named artifact and section. **Six
> required an artifact change** rather than a citation, because the honest answer was "no": CHK002,
> CHK012, CHK016, CHK027, CHK032, CHK036. Two more (CHK044, CHK045) were resolved by the
> `/speckit-analyze` remediation round. Each is annotated below with what changed. An item marked
> `[x]` on the strength of a citation that did not exist would defeat the purpose of the file.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all eight configuration proof obligations enumerated with individually decidable pass conditions, rather than as one general "configuration works" statement? [Completeness, Contract §C-C7] — **Yes.** C-C7 tabulates obligations 1–8, each a separate decidable row; tasks T016–T019 map to them one-to-one.
- [x] CHK002 Do the requirements state what evidence is sufficient to declare a proof obligation met — who records the result, and where it lives? [Gap] — **Was a real gap; now added.** C-C7 gained a *"What counts as evidence, and where it lives"* table: a named passing test in `proof_gate.rs` is the only sufficient evidence, recorded per obligation in research §D6 by T020, with a partial result defined as failure.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for the interval between the proof gate failing and the fallback adapter being accepted, so the system is not left in an unspecified state? [Gap, Research §D6] — **Yes, now explicit.** C-C7 closes with the rule that the surface is *unimplemented, not half-implemented*, in that interval; tasks Phase 5 header states the branch is selected once at T020 and re-derived nowhere.
- [x] CHK004 Are the declared-size ceilings and the traversal work budget specified as two separately-failing conditions with distinct diagnostics, rather than one "resource limit"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-039] — **Yes.** C-G1 separates the two families; C-G2 fails ceilings at Register on declared counts; C-G9 makes budget exhaustion an `Internal` defect signal distinct from every author-facing diagnostic.
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for **every** output path a secret value can reach, including the paths the underlying crate does not cover? [Completeness, Contract §C-C9] — **Yes.** C-C9's six-row table assigns each path an owner and marks the five the crate does not supply, `Display` included.
- [x] CHK006 Is the required content of the dependency inventory specified field by field, rather than as "record the dependencies"? [Completeness, Research §5] — **Yes.** Fields are version, licence, MSRV compatibility, advisory status, enabled features, duplicates (T030–T032), against the resolved `Cargo.lock`.
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements defined for what happens when a **transitive** dependency lacks the evidence FR-040 demands? [Coverage, Spec §FR-040] — **Yes.** T033 states the failing condition: the phase fails if *any* resolved package lacks it. Expressed as a failure, not an activity.
- [x] CHK008 Does the specification define the **deterministic outcome** of a repeated tracing bootstrap attempt, rather than only asserting it is "safe"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029] — **Yes.** A second call returns `AlreadyInstalled`; 0 panics, 0 silent successes, 0 silent replacements (C-O7, T097).
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for who may install the process-global subscriber, and is the prohibition on the library doing so stated normatively? [Completeness, Contract §C-O7] — **Yes.** C-O7 is titled "The library never owns the process-global subscriber" and carries a three-row API table; `Application::build()` installs nothing, proven by T098 installing one afterwards.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK010 Is "explicitly unstable" defined by what it **permits and forbids**, rather than by tone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036] — **Yes.** FR-036 forbids a semantic-versioning promise while the window is open and requires the statement in the surface's own published documentation; closure needs a named event plus a superseding record.
- [x] CHK011 Is the distinction between the work-budget **allowance** (2048 / 16384 / 18432) and the **expected observed** cost (2048 / 8192 / 10240) stated explicitly, so neither can be mistaken for the other? [Clarity, Contract §C-G4] — **Yes.** C-G4 tabulates observed cost against allowance and notes the edge axis sits at half its allowance.
- [x] CHK012 Is "examination" defined precisely enough that two independent implementations would count the same events? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-039] — **Was a real gap; now added.** C-G1 gained a normative *"What one examination is"* table fixing the increment points at iterator yield and explicitly excluding graph construction and diagnostic rendering.
- [x] CHK013 Is "source attribution" defined at a stated granularity — per key, per key path, or per layer? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016] — **Yes, per key path.** `ResolvedConfig.attribution: BTreeMap<KeyPath, SourceLayer>` (plan §Crate DAG property 5, data-model §2.6).
- [x] CHK014 Is "incompatible structural shape" defined by enumerated kinds (table / array / scalar) rather than left to the reader? [Clarity, Spec §FR-044] — **Yes.** FR-044 step 2(c) and C-C7 obligation 7 enumerate the kinds and require the failure to name **both** layers, with 0 coercions and 0 last-wins.
- [x] CHK015 Can "the first real transport adapter has exercised the surface and its feedback has been applied" be judged met or unmet by a reader who was not present when it happened? [Measurability, Spec §FR-036] — **Yes.** It is an *event* with an artefact — an adapter that exercised the surface — paired with an accepted superseding record. Both are inspectable after the fact; neither depends on having been present.
- [x] CHK016 Is "qualified independent review" defined with the criteria a reviewer must satisfy, rather than left to be decided when it is needed? [Ambiguity, Research §D11] — **Was a real gap; now added.** D11 gained a four-criterion table (a person; not the author; competent in the subject; able to reject), and records that criteria 1, 2, and 4 cannot be met by anyone available today — a staffing fact, which is what makes a waiver the correct instrument.
- [x] CHK017 Is "opaque" defined as a constraint on the identifier's **inputs** rather than on its appearance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-043] — **Yes.** FR-043 constrains inputs: one generation site, cryptographically secure random bytes and no other input. SC-019(a)–(c) verify inputs, never appearance.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK018 Do the work-budget figures agree across specification, plan, data model, provider-graph contract, and quickstart? [Consistency, Spec §FR-039] — **Yes, measured.** 2048 / 16384 / 18432 appear in all six artifacts including `tasks.md`; 0 occurrences of any near-miss value. The observed figure 10240 is absent from `spec.md` alone, correctly — the spec is implementation-free and 10240 is a property of the chosen algorithm.
- [x] CHK019 Do the configuration and observability requirements use one consistent term for a configuration source layer? [Consistency, Spec §FR-044] — **Yes.** `SourceLayer` is the single term, in FR-016/FR-044, C-C, the `ResolvedConfig` port, and the data model.
- [x] CHK020 Is the drain-budget default stated identically everywhere it appears? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006] — **Yes, measured.** **30 s** in spec FR-006/FR-042, plan, `lifecycle-contract.md` C-L, data-model (twice), and T060. 0 variants.
- [x] CHK021 Do the redaction obligations in the error taxonomy and the configuration contract impose the same duty, with neither implying the underlying crate covers more than it does? [Consistency, Contract §C-E3] — **Yes.** C-E3 states the crate supplies redacted `Debug` and zeroization, **implements no `Display` at all**, and reaches none of error messages, context, tracing fields, or serialization — and cross-references C-C9, which assigns the same five paths to Renvor.
- [x] CHK022 Are the crate-boundary requirements consistent with ADR-0002's re-export-only rule for the facade? [Consistency, Plan §Crate dependency DAG] — **Yes.** DAG property 3 requires `pub use` and 0 function bodies, `impl` blocks, or type definitions; T056 implements it and T101's Gate 13 asserts it with positive controls.
- [x] CHK023 Do the closure conditions for the instability window read identically in the clarification record, the requirement, the success criterion, and the dependencies list? [Consistency, Spec §SC-022] — **Yes, and now machine-checked.** SC-022 requires one byte-identical sentence across the 3 normative locations; **T104** adds that agreement check to `xtask`, so it is enforced rather than asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK024 Are the run-identifier criteria separated into **gating** and **non-gating**, with the non-gating status stated inside the criterion rather than only in commentary? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-019] — **Yes.** SC-019(b) and (c) are labelled *release-gating* in the criterion text; (d) is labelled *non-gating* in the criterion text.
- [x] CHK025 Can every success criterion be evaluated without executing a probabilistic test whose outcome varies by chance? [Measurability, Spec §SC-019] — **Yes.** SC-019(b) fixes the entropy and asserts purity, containing 0 probabilistic assertions; the only sampling check is (d), which 0 release gates depend on.
- [x] CHK026 Are the dependency-inventory pass conditions expressed as a **failing** condition, not only as a list of activities to perform? [Acceptance Criteria, Research §5] — **Yes.** T033 opens "Fail the phase if **any** resolved package lacks the evidence FR-040 requires".
- [x] CHK027 Is the recursion-depth obligation stated with the specific conditions under which it must hold — node count, thread kind, and stack size? [Measurability, Contract §C-G10] — **Was a real gap; now added.** C-G10 gained a six-row conditions table: 1024 nodes, a Tokio worker thread, stack pinned explicitly to **2 MiB** via `thread_stack_size` — verified from Tokio's own documentation, which states that default is *"subject to change in the future"*, which is precisely why it is pinned rather than inherited — and a failure meaning the recursive implementation is rejected, **not** that the ceiling is lowered.
- [x] CHK028 Do the zero-asserting criteria each name a positive control, so a zero cannot be produced by a check that never fired? [Acceptance Criteria, Quickstart §A note on fail-closed checks] — **Yes.** Quickstart §"A note on fail-closed checks" states the rule, and controls appear at Gates 1, 4, 6, 13 (five), and 14.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for the recovery path when the configuration proof gate fails — who decides, what is recorded, and what is blocked? [Coverage, Recovery Flow] — **Yes.** C-C7's evidence table names the decider (the test outcome), the record (research §D6 via T020), and the block (the fallback is custom infrastructure, so T029 gates it).
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for the case where the resolver's own fallback (an iterative SCC implementation) is triggered? [Coverage, Contract §C-G10] — **Yes.** C-G10 states the trigger in advance; T025 records it; `tasks.md` §Hard blocks places it under the same T029 ADR block.
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements defined for an ADR-0007 gate that is still unmet when the implementation is otherwise ready to merge? [Coverage, Exception Flow] — **Yes.** `tasks.md` §Hard blocks: T041 must not merge before T029, T054 depends on T041, and the Implementation Strategy states plainly that the MVP terminates at a governance decision rather than at a test run.
- [x] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a configuration source that is present but contributes no values? [Coverage, Edge Case] — **Was a real gap; now added.** New **C-C11** distinguishes *present and empty* from *absent* from *absent but required*, requires the distinction to survive into the attribution report, and forbids silent substitution of a zero value for a defaulted key.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK033 Is an environment variable set to an **empty string** distinguished, in the requirements, from one that is **unset**? [Edge Case, Contract §C-C3] — **Yes.** C-C3 and proof obligation 6 require `KEY=""` to **fail** rather than be reinterpreted as unset; the candidate crate's documented "treated as unset" is recorded as known negative evidence.
- [x] CHK034 Are requirements defined for a graph sitting **exactly at** each ceiling, not only above and below it? [Edge Case, Spec §SC-021] — **Yes.** C-G2 requires a graph **at both ceilings simultaneously** (1024 providers, 8192 edges) to succeed — "a ceiling that cannot be reached is a lower ceiling with a misleading number" — and SC-021 asserts 1024/8192 pass with 1025/8193 failing.
- [x] CHK035 Are requirements defined for a single provider declaring a dependency on itself? [Edge Case, Gap] — **Yes.** C-G8: a returned component with more than one node **or a single node carrying a self-edge** is a cycle. The self-edge case is named explicitly because a one-node SCC is otherwise the normal case.
- [x] CHK036 Are requirements defined for a secret value nested inside a collection or a nested table, rather than only at the top level? [Edge Case, Gap] — **Was a real gap; now added.** C-C9 gained a *"Nesting is not an exemption"* clause: redaction holds at any depth in every row of the output table, follows by construction from redaction being a property of the type, and is **tested at depth ≥ 2**.

- [x] CHK037 Is the **absence** of performance targets stated as a deliberate, reasoned decision rather than left as an omission a reader must interpret? [Completeness, Plan §Technical Context] — **Yes.** Plan §Technical Context: "**none declared, deliberately**" — no transport exists to measure against, and principle XII prohibits performance claims without measurement.
- [x] CHK038 Are platform support claims limited to what evidence exists, with the unclaimed platforms named explicitly? [Measurability, Plan §Technical Context] — **Yes.** Plan states Linux supported and tested; **macOS and Windows unclaimed** by name, because every workflow runs `ubuntu-latest` and the matrix varies toolchain only.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK039 Is the assumption that the direct-dependency evaluation predicts the **transitive** graph labelled as unvalidated rather than presented as an inventory? [Assumption, Research §3] — **Yes.** §3 is titled "Direct-dependency candidate evaluation" and opens with a block stating it is **NOT** the complete inventory FR-040 requires; T033 records whether it predicted the transitive graph accurately.
- [x] CHK040 Are the four recorded limitations of the candidate configuration crate traceable to primary sources rather than asserted? [Traceability, Research §D6] — **Yes.** Each of the four cites the crate's own documentation or source, including the `Option::or` combinator that discards the winning layer and the `Err(_) if is_empty => Ok(None)` fall-through.
- [x] CHK041 Is the assumption that the selected SCC implementation's traversal pattern stays stable across versions recorded, together with the consequence if it changes? [Assumption, Contract §C-G6] — **Yes.** C-G6 records that a changed traversal pattern would change the counters and the SC-021 assertions would **fail loudly** — "which is the intended behaviour, not a fragility". Counters are observed at a Renvor-owned trait boundary, never by reading the dependency's internals.

## Governance & Authority

- [x] CHK042 Do the requirements state which authority may accept ADR-0007, and name explicitly which existing waivers **cannot**? [Completeness, Research §D11] — **Yes.** D11 tabulates what W-002 and W-003 each cover and do **not** cover; T027 requires that non-authorisation to be written into the ADR itself; the authorising instrument is **W-004** and nothing else.
- [x] CHK043 Is the non-independence of every in-phase review stated as a binding constraint rather than as a caveat a reader may skip? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions] — **Yes.** Spec §Assumptions and plan both state every review produced inside this phase is **advisory and non-independent**; D11 adds that a waiver removes the *requirement*, never the *fact*.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK044 Is there an unresolved conflict between ADR-0003's dependency policy — which records that **reusable library crates do not commit a lockfile** — and FR-040, which requires dependency versions to be resolvable **from a committed lockfile**? The workspace currently tracks `Cargo.lock`, so one of the two statements does not describe this repository. [Conflict] — **Resolved in writing.** New research **§D12**: the table's two columns have different owners. Version requirements are per **crate** (compatible ranges, 0 exact pins — honoured literally); the lockfile is per **workspace**, because Cargo maintains exactly one, and this workspace contains `xtask`, which ADR-0003's *automation* row requires to commit one. Both statements stand; the automation row governs.
- [x] CHK045 Is it unambiguous whether `renvor` taken with **default features** is subject to the same dependency-isolation claim as `renvor-core`, or whether the isolation applies only to the core-only path? [Ambiguity, Plan §Crate dependency DAG] — **Resolved.** Plan DAG property 1 now states there is no third reading: `config` is **default-on**, so isolation is opt-in via `default-features = false` and the out-of-the-box footprint is the wider one. **T006** creates the feature and **T102** asserts both directions with a positive control, making the claim executable rather than stated.

- [x] CHK046 Is the **publishable crate set** defined for this phase, and is the Phase 001 release rehearsal still runnable against it? [Conflict] — **Added after the other 45 were resolved, because it was found by running a command rather than by reading an artifact.** `crates/renvor/Cargo.toml` asserted "No dependencies… declaring none is the strongest form of compliance"; Phase 002 gives the facade dependencies, and `cargo publish -p renvor --dry-run` then fails — **including when the dependency is marked publishable**, since the dependency must exist on the registry. Resolved in research **§D13** with a four-case experiment: the new crates become `publish = true` with complete metadata (**T001–T003**), the facade uses `{ path, version }` (**T006**), and the rehearsal moves to `--workspace` (**T007**, **T008**). Recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because it is the clearest instance of a checklist limit: **an artifact review cannot find a defect that only a running command exposes.**

**Traceability**: **43 of 46** items (**93%**) carry a section reference or an explicit
`[Gap]` / `[Conflict]` / `[Assumption]` / `[Ambiguity]` marker, above the 80% minimum. The three
without one — CHK029, CHK031, CHK032 — carry scenario-class markers (Recovery Flow, Exception
Flow, Edge Case) instead, which is deliberate: they ask whether a scenario class is covered at
all, so pointing them at a section would presuppose the answer.

**Soft cap exceeded, deliberately and on the record**: the skill sets a soft cap of 40 items and
directs prioritisation by risk when candidates exceed it. This file has **45**. The overage is
carried rather than trimmed because the request named **six** explicit focus areas — more than the
skill's four-cluster maximum — and each contributes items that cannot be merged without losing the
distinction that made it a focus area. Near-duplicates *were* merged: the eight configuration
obligations are one item (CHK001) rather than eight, and the five crate-DAG properties are two
(CHK022, CHK045) rather than five.

**Resolution outcome**: **46 of 46** resolved. **37** were answered by citing an artifact that
already covered them. **8** were not, and were fixed rather than argued away — CHK002, CHK012,
CHK016, CHK027, CHK032, CHK036 (artifact changes this round) and CHK044, CHK045 (the
`/speckit-analyze` remediation). The value of the checklist is concentrated in those eight: each
was a place where the artifacts read as though a question had been answered when it had not.
